One commenter called the 'Portable Computer' name very misleading. There is no device: you still subscribe to Perplexity's services, it's cloud infrastructure with transparent hardware, and Perplexity's orchestrator decides what gets escalated to the cloud. They had hoped for plug-and-play, privacy-focused agent hardware.

One commenter summarized the offering: "Computer" is Perplexity's cloud-hosted, multi-model harness/router, and "Portable Computer" lets you run that harness locally, but you must bring your own NVIDIA DGX Spark. They questioned why it is tied to the Spark rather than any system capable of local inference.
After viewing the demo page, one user said it looks very useful. They then noted that, despite advertising a local harness and models, it is closed source and requires a Pro or Max account.

One commenter questioned the target audience. Someone technical enough to buy a DGX Spark and self-host open-weight models would likely build the orchestrator themselves or use open-source tools rather than pay a Perplexity subscription.

One commenter saw it as just another local agent with cloud handoff, similar to Warp's local-to-cloud handoff. They felt Perplexity's value proposition and differentiation are slim or poorly communicated.

A Pro subscriber (via a promotion) found Perplexity generally poor. Specific models are often unavailable, context collapses after a few rounds, and Pro search is fast but superficial. They said it frequently routes them to Computer, which requires buying credits, and they saw this as upselling.

One commenter found the hybrid local/cloud architecture sensible and said it explains why Apple and NVIDIA might be interested in Perplexity. They noted Apple has long been thinking about hybrid compute.
A user complained that you need very expensive hardware (an NVIDIA DGX Spark) to run the Portable Computer version.

One user said the blog didn't clearly explain how to access Perplexity Computer. After refreshing perplexity.ai, they found a 'Computer' option in the sidebar (perplexity.ai/computer), but it required the $200/month Max subscription, which they didn't have.
